A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same autoregressive-buffer research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original computational benchmarks and predictive evaluations on synthetic functions, EEG, multisensory model comparison, and tabular regression, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds memory measurements, expanded tabular evaluations, and the experiments in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The cached-context/causal-buffer procedure, training objective, attention curriculum, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. The LBANP experiment implements the Perceiver-style extension already described in v1's architectural-generality discussion, without introducing a new buffer procedure.

E1.justification: Tabular evaluation expands from three time-series datasets to six, adding Jena Climate, Tetouan City power consumption, and California Housing Prices. This adds weather and housing coverage, including non-temporal regression; California Housing receives interpolation evaluation only. The original synthetic, EEG, and multisensory tasks remain.

E2.justification: Appendix H adds GP comparisons against a plain autoregressive Decoder Transformer and against independent and standard-AR LBANP modes (Figures A14 and A16). These are localized additions; the principal TNP and TabICL comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Tabular evaluation changes from N=128 to N=16 and 1024 in Table 3, with N=256 added in Table A6; M=32 and 16 sampled subsets remain. V2 also adds peak-memory and normalized-score measurements and new ablation configurations, including training with K=64. Appendix D.3.2 changes the reported log motor-noise prior from a truncated normal with mean 1.5 and SD 1.5 to mean 0 and SD 0.5; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects rerunning or correcting documentation.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds investigations of context permutation invariance, buffer positional embeddings, order-averaging sample counts, and LBANP compatibility. Its buffer-length study trains with maximum K=64, extending rather than duplicating v1's K=1,4,16 comparisons. Appendix C.6 also adds memory-scaling analysis.

E5.justification: H.3 newly examines Monte Carlo estimates using 2–128 target orderings, supplementing the retained default of 128. Main training-seed counts, evaluation repetitions, and mean/SEM practices remain unchanged. Table 2's caption drops v1's explicit identification of parenthesized uncertainties as SEMs.

E6.justification: Reported values in Tables 1–2 and A1–A5 are retained. V2 replaces the N=128 tabular results with different-context results and adds Tables A6–A7 and memory/ablation curves. New findings include reported 6–7-fold memory savings at N=1024 and GP scores of 2.51 (0.02) both with and without buffer positional embeddings. These additions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The method's factorizations, objective, complexity analysis, and Appendix A mathematics are retained. The newly numbered joint-density equation restates v1's inline expression; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains efficient joint inference through cached set conditioning and a causal buffer. V2 extends the abstract and introduction's efficiency claims to up to sevenfold lower memory usage and explicitly includes density evaluation alongside the up-to-20-fold sampling speedup.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new decoder comparison as evidence for context permutation invariance, argues that explicit buffer positions are unnecessary in the tested GP setting, and attributes LBANP gains to recent targets bypassing latent compression. It also more clearly acknowledges the EEG forecasting gap and qualifies when tabular autoregression helps. Existing long-buffer limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds access links for the three additional datasets and settings for new ablations, and revises the documented motor-noise prior. Most architecture, training, hardware, and code-release information is unchanged. Documentation is incompletely synchronized: D.5 still states N=128 and refers to three datasets despite listing six and reporting different context sizes.

R1.justification: Related work adds connections to masked-diffusion caching, any-order autoregression, and Partition Generative Models; the positional-embedding ablation adds relevant literature. TabICLv2 and Mitra are also newly cited. The change from Jingang et al. to Qu et al. for the original TabICL paper is a bibliographic correction, not a new comparator.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, method exposition, and discussion receive extensive editing. Three related-work subsections are consolidated, and much of the main text changes from likelihood terminology to predictive-density terminology. V2 also adds an ethics statement and reorganizes the expanded appendix material.

P2.justification: V2 Figure 1 combines the former Figure 3 timing plots with new memory and aggregate-performance panels. Figure 2 replaces the earlier overview and small mask illustration with an integrated sampling, density-evaluation, and training-mask diagram. Table 3 is substantially redesigned; Tables A6–A7 and Figures A13–A17 are added. V1's illustrative sample-path panels are removed.

improvement.justification: The new controls in Appendix H, implemented LBANP extension, broader tabular evaluations, and memory measurements strengthen support for the method's design and applicability. The integrated method diagram also improves explanation. These gains extend an already substantial empirical case rather than resolving a fundamental flaw. Their benefit is partly offset by the stale N=128 evaluation description and unexplained motor-noise-prior revision alongside unchanged multisensory results.
